title: Canary failover harness for Private VPC: Terraform-driven smoke tests & health orchestration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a Terraform-driven canary failover harness for Private (VPC) deployments that automates non-disruptive smoke tests, health checks, and rollback actions across two regions. The harness will be used by SREs and platform engineers to rehearse DR scenarios safely against reserved or ephemeral test capacity and to validate automation before customer-impacting runbooks are executed.
background: We currently have multi-region DR runbooks and periodic resilience rehearsals, but they require significant manual coordination and are hard to run in a repeatable, CI-friendly way for Private deployments. Private VPC environments add complexity (customer routing, network ACLs, KMS/HSM keys, private control plane) so we need a test harness that simulates real failovers while minimizing blast radius.
proposed_solution: Build a reusable Terraform module plus a small orchestration lambda/container that will:
proposed_solution_details: Provision ephemeral test VPCs and minimal compute stacks in two target regions using the private-deploy Terraform modules (uses feature flags to avoid touching production resources)
Deploy a 'canary control-plane' variant of the private control plane with read-only data access and synthetic model shards (no customer data)
Implement traffic steering using Route53 weighted records + health checks to simulate primary->secondary switchover
Run a sequence of smoke tests: API handshake, token auth, KV cache warm-up, short generation flows, embedding checks, and metrics emission verification
On failure, capture full diagnostics (logs, heap snapshots, db traces), trigger an automated rollback, and create a pre-populated incident with remediation checklist
Expose a CI job that runs the harness nightly and on demand, with results posted to a DR dashboard and Slack channel
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module can provision ephemeral test stacks in two regions with a single 'plan+apply' CI step
Canary can be induced to fail primary region and observe automated traffic shift to secondary without manual DNS edits
Smoke tests run end-to-end within the harness and report pass/fail to the DR dashboard
Failure cases produce a diagnostic bundle and an auto-created incident ticket with links to artifacts
Runbook steps for SRE manual escalation are generated and validated during a dry-run
No customer data or production keys are used in any test runs; KMS/HSM interactions are simulated or use dedicated test keys
tasks: Design Terraform module interface for ephemeral test stacks (variables: region pair, instance profile, test-key-id)
Implement orchestration service (small container) to execute failover sequence and smoke tests
Add Route53 health-check templates and weighted record automation to Terraform module
Create smoke test suite (curl SDK flows, embedding/latency assertions, metrics emit checks)
Wire CI job and schedule (GitHub Actions / Jenkins) and a Slack/Webhook notifier
Integrate diagnostic bundle collector and incident creation via Jira/Linear API
Write canary runbook and on-call playbook; add to Confluence; run tabletop with SRE and Platform
progress_updates: 2026-02-16 — Kickoff: scoped requirements with SRE/Platform/PM. Confirmed constraints around KMS usage and no production network changes.
2026-02-22 — Terraform module scaffold completed (initial variables + provider configs). PR created: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/2468
2026-03-01 — Smoke test harness prototype implemented in Go. Basic API handshake and short generation test passing in dev region.
2026-03-05 — Orchestration container can toggle Route53 weighted records in sandbox; verified health-check toggles cause expected traffic move
2026-03-09 — CI job added to run nightly canaries. First scheduled run failed due to IAM role missing sts:AssumeRole for cross-account test; mitigation: create ephemeral role; pending security review
2026-03-10 — Security review requested and initial comments received: need to ensure test KMS keys use dedicated test key policy and HSM usage is simulated. Reassigning to security follow-up task.
risks: Accidentally touching production VPCs or routes if variable is misconfigured — mitigation: strict naming, safeguards in module, and a 'dry-run' mode
KMS/HSM interactions could be rejected by security policy — mitigation: use dedicated test keys and request exception for CI service account
DNS caching could delay observable traffic shift — mitigation: use low TTL test zones and explicit cache-flush steps in test harness
Ephemeral cost for nightly runs — mitigation: limit run frequency and re-use small instance types for canaries
open_questions: Should the harness support on-prem private deployments (air-gapped)? That will require a different provisioning approach
What is the minimum SLO coverage we must validate in canary (p50/p95/p99/tokens-per-second)?
Who owns the incident auto-created by the harness for follow-up? SRE or Platform? Recommend SRE as owner with Platform notified
